title: Measuring the Unreachable: The Secret of Trigonometry
body:
How did ancient astronomers calculate the distance from Earth to the Moon without a tape measure? How did Radhanath Sikdar and Sir George Everest calculate the exact height of Mount Everest (8,848 m) without ever climbing to its peak?

The answer lies in **Trigonometry (त्रिकोणमिति / ત્રિકોણમિતિ)** — derived from the Greek words *tri* (three), *gon* (sides), and *metron* (measure). It is the branch of mathematics that explores the profound relationship between the angles and lengths of sides in triangles.

Whenever you cannot physically climb or reach an object — whether it is the tip of a cellular antenna, the height of a sky-piercing pyramid, or the width of a roaring river — trigonometry allows you to measure it using a simple angle of sight and a baseline distance!
title_hi: पहुँच से बाहर की माप: त्रिकोणमिति का रहस्य
body_hi:
प्राचीन खगोलविदों ने बिना किसी फीते के पृथ्वी से चंद्रमा की दूरी की गणना कैसे की? राधानाथ सिकदर और सर जॉर्ज एवरेस्ट ने बिना चोटी पर चढ़े माउंट एवरेस्ट की सटीक ऊँचाई (8,848 मीटर) की गणना कैसे की?

इसका उत्तर है **त्रिकोणमिति (Trigonometry)** — जो ग्रीक शब्दों *त्रि* (तीन), *गोन* (भुजाएँ) और *मेट्रॉन* (माप) से मिलकर बना है। यह गणित की वह शाखा है जो त्रिभुजों के कोणों और उनकी भुजाओं की लंबाइयों के बीच के गहरे संबंध का अध्ययन करती है।

जब भी आप किसी वस्तु पर शारीरिक रूप से नहीं चढ़ सकते — चाहे वह मोबाइल टॉवर का शिखर हो, आकाश छूते पिरामिड की ऊँचाई हो, या किसी विशाल नदी की चौड़ाई — त्रिकोणमिति केवल दृष्टि कोण और जमीन पर मापी गई दूरी की सहायता से सटीक गणना करने की शक्ति देती है!

question: Think Carefully: If you have a small right triangle with a 30° angle, and another giant right triangle also with a 30° angle (whose sides are 10 times longer), what happens to the ratio of the side opposite to 30° divided by the hypotenuse?
options: The ratio remains exactly the same in both triangles
The ratio becomes 10 times larger in the giant triangle
The ratio becomes 10 times smaller in the giant triangle
The ratio depends on the area of the triangle
explanation: By AAA similarity criterion, all right-angled triangles with the same acute angle (here 30°) are similar to each other! Therefore, the ratios of their corresponding sides are constant, regardless of the size of the triangle. This constant ratio is the foundation of Trigonometry!

title: Discovery: Identifying Sides Relative to the Angle of Interest
body:
In a right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$, right-angled at $B$:

1. **Hypotenuse (कर्ण / કર્ણ):** The longest side, always opposite to the $90^\circ$ right angle ($AC$).
2. **Opposite Side (सम्मुख भुजा / સામેની બાજુ):** The side directly opposite to the angle you are looking at. For angle $A$, the opposite side is $BC$.
3. **Adjacent Side (संलग्न भुजा / પાસેની બાજુ):** The side next to the angle (other than the hypotenuse). For angle $A$, the adjacent side is $AB$.

**CRITICAL PERSPECTIVE SHIFT:**
If you shift your perspective to angle $C$:
- The opposite side of $\angle C$ is $AB$!
- The adjacent side of $\angle C$ is $BC$!
- The hypotenuse $AC$ never changes.

*Never think of 'base' and 'perpendicular' as fixed vertical or horizontal lines! They depend entirely on which acute angle you are observing.*
title_hi: खोज: अभीष्ट कोण के सापेक्ष भुजाओं की सही पहचान
body_hi:
समकोण त्रिभुज $\triangle ABC$ में, जिसका कोण $B$ समकोण है:

1. **कर्ण (Hypotenuse):** सबसे लंबी भुजा, जो हमेशा $90^\circ$ समकोण के सम्मुख होती है ($AC$)।
2. **सम्मुख भुजा (Opposite Side):** वह भुजा जो आपके द्वारा देखे जा रहे कोण के ठीक सामने होती है। कोण $A$ के लिए सम्मुख भुजा $BC$ है।
3. **संलग्न भुजा (Adjacent Side):** वह भुजा जो कोण के साथ लगी होती है (कर्ण को छोड़कर)। कोण $A$ के लिए संलग्न भुजा $AB$ है।

**दृष्टिकोण का महत्वपूर्ण परिवर्तन:**
यदि आप अपना ध्यान कोण $C$ पर ले जाते हैं:
- $\angle C$ की सम्मुख भुजा $AB$ बन जाती है!
- $\angle C$ की संलग्न भुजा $BC$ बन जाती है!
- कर्ण $AC$ कभी नहीं बदलता।

*कभी भी 'आधार' और 'लंब' को निश्चित क्षैतिज या ऊर्ध्वाधर रेखाएँ न मानें! वे पूरी तरह इस बात पर निर्भर करते हैं कि आप किस न्यूनकोण के दृष्टिकोण से देख रहे हैं।*

body_gu:
કાટકોણ ત્રિકોણ $\triangle ABC$ માં, જ્યાં ખૂણો $B$ કાટખૂણો છે:

1. **કર્ણ (Hypotenuse):** સૌથી મોટી બાજુ, જે હંમેશા $90^\circ$ કાટખૂણાની સામે આવેલી હોય છે ($AC$).
2. **સામેની બાજુ (Opposite Side):** તમે જે ખૂણાને સંદર્ભ તરીકે લો છો તેની બરાબર સામેની બાજુ. ખૂણા $A$ માટે સામેની બાજુ $BC$ છે.
3. **પાસેની બાજુ (Adjacent Side):** ખૂણા સાથે જોડાયેલી બાજુ (કર્ણ સિવાયની). ખૂણા $A$ માટે પાસેની બાજુ $AB$ છે.

**ખૂબ જ મહત્વનો ફેરફાર:**
જો તમે ખૂણા $C$ ના સંદર્ભમાં વિચાર કરો:
- $\angle C$ ની સામેની બાજુ $AB$ બને છે!
- $\angle C$ ની પાસેની બાજુ $BC$ બને છે!
- કર્ણ $AC$ ક્યારેય બદલાતો નથી.

*ક્યારેય 'પાયો' કે 'વેધ' ને સ્થિર ન માનો! તે સંપૂર્ણપણે તમે કયો લઘુકોણ ધ્યાનમાં લો છો તેના પર આધારિત છે.*

title: The Six Trigonometric Ratios: Definitions & Relationships
body:
For an acute angle $A$ in right triangle $\triangle ABC$ (right-angled at $B$):

### 1. The Three Primary Ratios
- **Sine of $\angle A$ (sin A):** $\frac{\text{Side opposite to } \angle A}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{BC}{AC}$
- **Cosine of $\angle A$ (cos A):** $\frac{\text{Side adjacent to } \angle A}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{AB}{AC}$
- **Tangent of $\angle A$ (tan A):** $\frac{\text{Side opposite to } \angle A}{\text{Side adjacent to } \angle A} = \frac{BC}{AB}$

### 2. The Three Reciprocal Ratios
- **Cosecant of $\angle A$ (cosec A):** $\frac{1}{\sin A} = \frac{\text{Hypotenuse}}{\text{Side opposite to } \angle A} = \frac{AC}{BC}$
- **Secant of $\angle A$ (sec A):** $\frac{1}{\cos A} = \frac{\text{Hypotenuse}}{\text{Side adjacent to } \angle A} = \frac{AC}{AB}$
- **Cotangent of $\angle A$ (cot A):** $\frac{1}{\tan A} = \frac{\text{Side adjacent to } \angle A}{\text{Side opposite to } \angle A} = \frac{AB}{BC}$

### 3. Quotient Relations
$$\tan A = \frac{\sin A}{\cos A}, \quad \cot A = \frac{\cos A}{\sin A}$$

*Notation Note:* $(\sin A)^2$ is written as $\sin^2 A$, NOT $\sin A^2$. Also, $\sin A$ is NOT $\sin \times A$; 'sin' has no meaning without an angle.
title_hi: छह त्रिकोणमितीय अनुपात: परिभाषाएँ और पारस्परिक संबंध
body_hi:
समकोण त्रिभुज $\triangle ABC$ में न्यूनकोण $A$ के लिए (जहाँ $B$ समकोण है):

### 1. तीन प्राथमिक अनुपात
- **Sine (sin A):** $\frac{\text{कोण } A \text{ की सम्मुख भुजा}}{\text{कर्ण}} = \frac{BC}{AC}$
- **Cosine (cos A):** $\frac{\text{कोण } A \text{ की संलग्न भुजा}}{\text{कर्ण}} = \frac{AB}{AC}$
- **Tangent (tan A):** $\frac{\text{कोण } A \text{ की सम्मुख भुजा}}{\text{कोण } A \text{ की संलग्न भुजा}} = \frac{BC}{AB}$

### 2. तीन व्युत्क्रम अनुपात
- **Cosecant (cosec A):** $\frac{1}{\sin A} = \frac{\text{कर्ण}}{\text{सम्मुख भुजा}} = \frac{AC}{BC}$
- **Secant (sec A):** $\frac{1}{\cos A} = \frac{\text{कर्ण}}{\text{संलग्न भुजा}} = \frac{AC}{AB}$
- **Cotangent (cot A):** $\frac{1}{\tan A} = \frac{\text{संलग्न भुजा}}{\text{सम्मुख भुजा}} = \frac{AB}{BC}$

### 3. भागफल संबंध
$$\tan A = \frac{\sin A}{\cos A}, \quad \cot A = \frac{\cos A}{\sin A}$$

*संकेतन नियम:* $(\sin A)^2$ को $\sin^2 A$ लिखा जाता है, $\sin A^2$ नहीं। साथ ही, $\sin A$ का अर्थ $\sin \times A$ नहीं है; कोण के बिना 'sin' का कोई स्वतंत्र अस्तित्व नहीं है।
title_gu: છ ત્રિકોણમિતીય ગુણોત્તરો: વ્યાખ્યાઓ અને પરસ્પર સંબંધો
body_gu:
કાટકોણ ત્રિકોણ $\triangle ABC$ માં લઘુકોણ $A$ માટે (જ્યાં $B$ કાટખૂણો છે):

### 1. ત્રણ મુખ્ય ગુણોત્તરો
- **Sine (sin A):** $\frac{\angle A \text{ ની સામેની બાજુ}}{\text{કર્ણ}} = \frac{BC}{AC}$
- **Cosine (cos A):** $\frac{\angle A \text{ ની પાસેની બાજુ}}{\text{કર્ણ}} = \frac{AB}{AC}$
- **Tangent (tan A):** $\frac{\angle A \text{ ની સામેની બાજુ}}{\angle A \text{ ની પાસેની બાજુ}} = \frac{BC}{AB}$

### 2. ત્રણ વ્યસ્ત ગુણોત્તરો
- **Cosecant (cosec A):** $\frac{1}{\sin A} = \frac{\text{કર્ણ}}{\text{સામેની બાજુ}} = \frac{AC}{BC}$
- **Secant (sec A):** $\frac{1}{\cos A} = \frac{\text{કર્ણ}}{\text{પાસેની બાજુ}} = \frac{AC}{AB}$
- **Cotangent (cot A):** $\frac{1}{\tan A} = \frac{\text{પાસેની બાજુ}}{\text{સામેની બાજુ}} = \frac{AB}{BC}$

### 3. ભાગાકાર સંબંધો
$$\tan A = \frac{\sin A}{\cos A}, \quad \cot A = \frac{\cos A}{\sin A}$$

*ગાણિતિક સંકેત:* $(\sin A)^2$ ને $\sin^2 A$ લખાય છે, $\sin A^2$ નહીં. વળી, $\sin A$ નો અર્થ $\sin \times A$ નથી; ખૂણા વગર 'sin' નો કોઈ સ્વતંત્ર અર્થ નથી.

title: Teacher Tip: The Magic Mnemonics for Trigonometric Ratios
body:
To remember the ratios instantly, Indian and Global students use these unforgettable mnemonics:

**English: SOH CAH TOA**
- **SOH:** $\sin = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}$
- **CAH:** $\cos = \frac{\text{Adjacent}}{\text{Hypotenuse}}$
- **TOA:** $\tan = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}}$

**Hindi: पंडित बद्री प्रसाद हर हर बोले (PBP / HHB)**
- $\sin = P/H$ (पंडित / हर)
- $\cos = B/H$ (बद्री / हर)
- $\tan = P/B$ (प्रसाद / बोले)

**Gujarati: સાક પાક સાપા**
- $\sin = \text{સા/ક}$ (સામેની બાજુ / કર્ણ)
- $\cos = \text{પા/ક}$ (પાસેની બાજુ / કર્ણ)

title: NCERT Example 2: Equal Sine Ratios Imply Equal Angles
body:
**Problem:** If $\angle B$ and $\angle Q$ are acute angles such that $\sin B = \sin Q$, then prove that $\angle B = \angle Q$.

**Proof:**
Consider two right triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle PQR$ where $\angle C = \angle R = 90^\circ$.
Given: $\sin B = \sin Q \implies \frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{PR}{PQ} = k$.
So $AC = k \cdot PR$ and $AB = k \cdot PQ$.
By Pythagoras theorem:
$$BC = \sqrt{AB^2 - AC^2}, \quad QR = \sqrt{PQ^2 - PR^2}$$
$$\frac{BC}{QR} = \frac{\sqrt{k^2 PQ^2 - k^2 PR^2}}{\sqrt{PQ^2 - PR^2}} = \frac{k\sqrt{PQ^2 - PR^2}}{\sqrt{PQ^2 - PR^2}} = k$$
Since $\frac{AC}{PR} = \frac{AB}{PQ} = \frac{BC}{QR} = k$, by SSS similarity criterion, $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR$.
Corresponding angles are equal: $\angle B = \angle Q$.

question: NCERT Example 5: In △OPQ, right-angled at P, OP = 7 cm and OQ - PQ = 1 cm. Determine the values of sin Q and cos Q.

(1 + PQ)² = OP² + PQ²
1 + 2PQ + PQ² = 7² + PQ²
1 + 2PQ = 49 ⇒ 2PQ = 48 ⇒ PQ = 24 cm.
OQ = 1 + 24 = 25 cm.
For angle Q: opposite side = OP = 7 cm, adjacent = PQ = 24 cm, hypotenuse = OQ = 25 cm.
Thus, sin Q = OP/OQ = 7/25, cos Q = PQ/OQ = 24/25.

title: Exercise 8.1 Q6: If cos A = cos B, Show That ∠A = ∠B
body:
**Problem:** If $\angle A$ and $\angle B$ are acute angles such that $\cos A = \cos B$, then show that $\angle A = \angle B$.

**Solution:**
Consider right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$, where $\angle C = 90^\circ$.
From definition of cosine:
$$\cos A = \frac{\text{Side adjacent to } \angle A}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{AC}{AB}$$
$$\cos B = \frac{\text{Side adjacent to } \angle B}{\text{Hypotenuse}} = \frac{BC}{AB}$$

Given $\cos A = \cos B$:
$$\frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{BC}{AB} \implies AC = BC$$

In $\triangle ABC$, since sides opposite to equal angles are equal (or angles opposite to equal sides are equal):
$$AC = BC \implies \angle B = \angle A$$
Hence, $\angle A = \angle B$. Proved!
title_hi: प्रश्नावली 8.1 Q6: यदि cos A = cos B, तो दर्शाइए कि ∠A = ∠B

**हल:**
समकोण त्रिभुज $\triangle ABC$ लीजिए जिसका कोण $C$ समकोण ($90^\circ$) है।
कोसाइन की परिभाषा से:
$$\cos A = \frac{AC}{AB}, \quad \cos B = \frac{BC}{AB}$$

दिया है $\cos A = \cos B$:
$$\frac{AC}{AB} = \frac{BC}{AB} \implies AC = BC$$

किसी त्रिभुज में समान भुजाओं के सम्मुख कोण बराबर होते हैं:
$$AC = BC \implies \angle B = \angle A$$
अतः $\angle A = \angle B$ सिद्ध हुआ!

question: Exercise 8.1 Q7: If cot θ = 7/8, evaluate: (i) (1 + sin θ)(1 - sin θ) / [(1 + cos θ)(1 - cos θ)], (ii) cot²θ.

Since 1 - sin²θ = cos²θ and 1 - cos²θ = sin²θ:

(ii) cot²θ = (7/8)² = 49/64. Both answers are 49/64!

title: Exercise 8.1 Q11: Conceptual True / False Analysis
body:
### Exercise 8.1 Question 11: State whether the following are true or false with justification:

1. **The value of tan A is always less than 1.**
   - **FALSE.** In a right triangle, the opposite side can be longer than the adjacent side (e.g., 4/3 = 1.33 > 1). Also $\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.732 > 1$.

2. **sec A = 12/5 for some value of angle A.**
   - **TRUE.** Since $\sec A = \text{Hypotenuse}/\text{Adjacent}$ and the hypotenuse is always the longest side, $\sec A \ge 1$. Here $12/5 = 2.4 > 1$, which is valid.

3. **cos A is the abbreviation used for the cosecant of angle A.**
   - **FALSE.** $\cos A$ is the abbreviation for the **cosine** of angle $A$. The abbreviation for cosecant is $\operatorname{cosec} A$.

4. **cot A is the product of cot and A.**
   - **FALSE.** $\cot A$ is the cotangent of the angle $A$. 'cot' separated from $A$ has no mathematical meaning.

5. **sin θ = 4/3 for some angle θ.**
   - **FALSE.** $\sin \theta = \text{Opposite}/\text{Hypotenuse}$. Since the hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle, the opposite side can never exceed the hypotenuse. Thus, $\sin \theta \le 1$. But $4/3 = 1.33 > 1$, which is impossible.
title_hi: प्रश्नावली 8.1 Q11: वैचारिक सत्य/असत्य विश्लेषण
body_hi:
### प्रश्नावली 8.1 प्रश्न 11: कारण सहित बताइए कि कथन सत्य हैं या असत्य:

1. **tan A का मान सदैव 1 से कम होता है।**
   - **असत्य।** समकोण त्रिभुज में सम्मुख भुजा संलग्न भुजा से बड़ी हो सकती है (जैसे 4/3 = 1.33 > 1)। $\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.732 > 1$ होता है।

2. **कोण A के किसी मान के लिए sec A = 12/5 हो सकता है।**
   - **सत्य।** चूँकि $\sec A = \text{कर्ण}/\text{संलग्न भुजा}$ और कर्ण सबसे लंबी भुजा होती है, अतः $\sec A \ge 1$ होना चाहिए। यहाँ $12/5 = 2.4 > 1$ है, जो संभव है।

3. **cos A, कोण A के cosecant के लिए प्रयुक्त एक संक्षिप्त रूप है।**
   - **असत्य।** $\cos A$ कोण $A$ के **cosine** का संक्षिप्त रूप है। Cosecant का संक्षिप्त रूप $\operatorname{cosec} A$ होता है।

4. **cot A, cot और A का गुणनफल होता है।**
   - **असत्य।** $\cot A$ कोण $A$ का कोटैंजेंट है। कोण $A$ से अलग होने पर 'cot' का कोई गणितीय अर्थ नहीं होता।

5. **किसी भी कोण θ के लिए sin θ = 4/3 हो सकता है।**
   - **असत्य।** $\sin \theta = \text{लंब}/\text{कर्ण}$। समकोण त्रिभुज में कर्ण सबसे लंबी भुजा होती है, इसलिए लंब कभी कर्ण से बड़ा नहीं हो सकता। अतः $\sin \theta \le 1$ होना चाहिए, जबकि $4/3 > 1$ है।

body_gu:
### સ્વાધ્યાય 8.1 પ્રશ્ન 11: કારણ આપી જણાવો કે નીચેના વિધાનો ખરા છે કે ખોટા:

1. **tan A નું મૂલ્ય હંમેશા 1 કરતાં ઓછું હોય છે.**
   - **ખોટું.** કાટકોણ ત્રિકોણમાં સામેની બાજુ પાસેની બાજુ કરતાં મોટી હોઈ શકે છે (દા.ત. 4/3 = 1.33 > 1). વળી $\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.732 > 1$ છે.

2. **ખૂણા A ના કોઈ મૂલ્ય માટે sec A = 12/5 હોઈ શકે.**
   - **ખરું.** $\sec A = \text{કર્ણ}/\text{પાસેની બાજુ}$ અને કર્ણ હંમેશા સૌથી મોટી બાજુ હોવાથી $\sec A \ge 1$ હોવો જોઈએ. અહીં $12/5 = 2.4 > 1$ હોવાથી શક્ય છે.

3. **cos A એ ખૂણા A ના cosecant માટે વપરાતું સંક્ષિપ્ત રૂપ છે.**
   - **ખોટું.** $\cos A$ એ ખૂણા $A$ ના **cosine** નું સંક્ષિપ્ત રૂપ છે. Cosecant નું સંક્ષિપ્ત રૂપ $\operatorname{cosec} A$ છે.

4. **cot A એ cot અને A નો ગુણાકાર છે.**
   - **ખોટું.** $\cot A$ એ ખૂણા $A$ નો કોટેન્જન્ટ છે. $A$ વિના 'cot' નો કોઈ સ્વતંત્ર ગાણિતિક અર્થ નથી.

5. **કોઈ ખૂણા θ માટે sin θ = 4/3 શક્ય છે.**
   - **ખોટું.** $\sin \theta = \text{સામેની બાજુ}/\text{કર્ણ}$. કાટકોણ ત્રિકોણમાં કર્ણ સૌથી મોટી બાજુ હોવાથી સામેની બાજુ ક્યારેય કર્ણ કરતાં મોટી ન હોઈ શકે. તેથી $\sin \theta \le 1$ જ હોય, જ્યારે $4/3 > 1$ છે.

title: The Geometry of Special Angles: Why 30°, 45°, and 60°?
body:
Why are angles like $30^\circ$, $45^\circ$, and $60^\circ$ the superstar angles of engineering and architecture? 

Because they originate directly from the two most symmetrical polygons in nature:
1. **The Square:** Cut diagonally in half, a square creates a $45^\circ - 45^\circ - 90^\circ$ triangle.

title: Discovery: Deriving Values for 45°, 30°, and 60°
body:
### 1. Ratios of 45° (Isosceles Right Triangle)
Consider an isosceles right triangle with base = $a$ and height = $a$.
By Pythagoras theorem, Hypotenuse = $\sqrt{a^2 + a^2} = a\sqrt{2}$.
$$\sin 45^\circ = \frac{a}{a\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \quad \cos 45^\circ = \frac{a}{a\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \quad \tan 45^\circ = \frac{a}{a} = 1$$

### 2. Ratios of 30° and 60° (Equilateral Triangle)
Consider an equilateral triangle $ABC$ with each side of length $2a$. Draw altitude $AD \perp BC$.
Then $BD = a$, and $\angle BAD = 30^\circ$, $\angle B = 60^\circ$.
By Pythagoras theorem: $AD = \sqrt{(2a)^2 - a^2} = \sqrt{3a^2} = a\sqrt{3}$.
- **For 30°:** Opposite = $BD = a$, Adjacent = $AD = a\sqrt{3}$, Hypotenuse = $2a$.
  $$\sin 30^\circ = \frac{a}{2a} = \frac{1}{2}, \quad \cos 30^\circ = \frac{a\sqrt{3}}{2a} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \quad \tan 30^\circ = \frac{a}{a\sqrt{3}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$
- **For 60°:** Opposite = $AD = a\sqrt{3}$, Adjacent = $BD = a$, Hypotenuse = $2a$.
  $$\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \quad \cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}, \quad \tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3}$$

### 3. Limiting Cases: 0° and 90°
- As angle $\theta \to 0^\circ$, Opposite side shrinks to $0$ and Adjacent side approaches Hypotenuse. Thus $\sin 0^\circ = 0, \cos 0^\circ = 1, \tan 0^\circ = 0$.
- As angle $\theta \to 90^\circ$, Adjacent side shrinks to $0$ and Opposite side equals Hypotenuse. Thus $\sin 90^\circ = 1, \cos 90^\circ = 0, \tan 90^\circ = \text{Not Defined}$.

### Complete Trigonometric Table

1. **sin θ increases** from $0$ to $1$ as $\theta$ increases from $0^\circ$ to $90^\circ$.
2. **cos θ decreases** from $1$ to $0$ as $\theta$ increases from $0^\circ$ to $90^\circ$.
3. At $\theta = 45^\circ$, $\sin 45^\circ = \cos 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\tan 45^\circ = \cot 45^\circ = 1$.
4. Notice that the $\cos$ row is simply the $\sin$ row written in reverse order!

title: Teacher Tip: The 5-Finger Palm Trick to Recreate the Table in 5 Seconds
body:
Forget rote memorization! Open your left hand facing you:
- **Thumb:** $0^\circ$
- **Index Finger:** $30^\circ$
- **Middle Finger:** $45^\circ$
- **Ring Finger:** $60^\circ$
- **Little Finger:** $90^\circ$

### The Golden Formulas:
$$\sin \theta = \frac{\sqrt{\text{Number of fingers BELOW}}}{2}$$
$$\cos \theta = \frac{\sqrt{\text{Number of fingers ABOVE}}}{2}$$
$$\tan \theta = \sqrt{\frac{\text{Fingers BELOW}}{\text{Fingers ABOVE}}}$$

*Quick Check for 60° (Ring Finger):*
- Fingers below = 3 (Thumb, Index, Middle) $\implies \sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
- Fingers above = 1 (Little finger) $\implies \cos 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{1}}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$.
- $\tan 60^\circ = \sqrt{3/1} = \sqrt{3}$. Instant and 100% foolproof in exams!

title: Exercise 8.2 Q4: Conceptual True / False Analysis
body:
### Exercise 8.2 Question 4: State whether the following are true or false with justification:

1. **sin(A + B) = sin A + sin B.**
   - **FALSE.** Let $A = 30^\circ, B = 60^\circ$.
     $\text{LHS} = \sin(30^\circ + 60^\circ) = \sin 90^\circ = 1$.
     $\text{RHS} = \sin 30^\circ + \sin 60^\circ = 1/2 + \sqrt{3}/2 = \frac{1 + \sqrt{3}}{2} \ne 1$.

2. **The value of sin θ increases as θ increases.**
   - **TRUE.** For acute angles ($0^\circ \le \theta \le 90^\circ$):
     $\sin 0^\circ = 0, \sin 30^\circ = 0.5, \sin 45^\circ = 0.707, \sin 60^\circ = 0.866, \sin 90^\circ = 1$. It strictly increases.

3. **The value of cos θ increases as θ increases.**
   - **FALSE.** For acute angles ($0^\circ \le \theta \le 90^\circ$):
     $\cos 0^\circ = 1, \cos 30^\circ = 0.866, \cos 45^\circ = 0.707, \cos 60^\circ = 0.5, \cos 90^\circ = 0$. It decreases from 1 to 0.

4. **sin θ = cos θ for all values of θ.**
   - **FALSE.** It is ONLY true when $\theta = 45^\circ$ (where both equal $1/\sqrt{2}$). For $\theta = 30^\circ$, $\sin 30^\circ = 1/2 \ne \cos 30^\circ = \sqrt{3}/2$.

5. **cot A is not defined for A = 0°.**
   - **TRUE.** $\cot 0^\circ = \frac{\cos 0^\circ}{\sin 0^\circ} = \frac{1}{0}$, which is undefined (division by zero).

title: The Power of Identities: Mathematical Truths that Never Fail
body:
What is the difference between an **Equation** and an **Identity**?

- An equation like $2x + 1 = 7$ is true for only ONE specific value of $x$ ($x = 3$).
- An algebraic identity like $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$ is true for **EVERY POSSIBLE NUMBER** you substitute into it!

Similarly, a **Trigonometric Identity (त्रिकोणमितीय सर्वसमिका / ત્રિકોણમિતીય નિત્યસમ)** is an equation involving trigonometric ratios of an angle that holds true for **every single angle $\theta$** for which the ratios are defined.

Mastering identities is like holding an algebraic key: you can transform complicated expressions into elegant, simple numbers, solve calculus problems, and prove breathtaking geometric relations!

title: Discovery: Deriving the 3 Master Pythagorean Identities
body:
Let us take a right-angled triangle $\triangle ABC$ right-angled at $B$. By the Pythagoras Theorem:
$$AB^2 + BC^2 = AC^2 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

### Identity 1: Dividing Eq. 1 by $AC^2$
$$\frac{AB^2}{AC^2} + \frac{BC^2}{AC^2} = \frac{AC^2}{AC^2} \implies \left(\frac{AB}{AC}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{BC}{AC}\right)^2 = 1$$
Since $\frac{BC}{AC} = \sin A$ and $\frac{AB}{AC} = \cos A$:
$$\mathbf{\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A = 1} \quad (\text{True for all } 0^\circ \le A \le 90^\circ)$$

### Identity 2: Dividing Eq. 1 by $AB^2$
$$\frac{AB^2}{AB^2} + \frac{BC^2}{AB^2} = \frac{AC^2}{AB^2} \implies 1 + \left(\frac{BC}{AB}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{AC}{AB}\right)^2$$
$$\mathbf{1 + \tan^2 A = \sec^2 A} \quad (\text{True for } 0^\circ \le A < 90^\circ)$$

### Identity 3: Dividing Eq. 1 by $BC^2$
$$\frac{AB^2}{BC^2} + \frac{BC^2}{BC^2} = \frac{AC^2}{BC^2} \implies \left(\frac{AB}{BC}\right)^2 + 1 = \left(\frac{AC}{BC}\right)^2$$
$$\mathbf{1 + \cot^2 A = \operatorname{cosec}^2 A} \quad (\text{True for } 0^\circ < A \le 90^\circ)$$

title: The Transformed Shapes of Identities for Fast Problem Solving
body:
Every identity has equivalent algebraic rearrangements that you must recognize instantly:

### 1. From $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$:
- $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta = (1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)$
- $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta = (1 - \sin\theta)(1 + \sin\theta)$

### 2. From $1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta$:
- $\sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1$
- $(\sec\theta - \tan\theta)(\sec\theta + \tan\theta) = 1 \implies \sec\theta - \tan\theta = \frac{1}{\sec\theta + \tan\theta}$
*(Very popular in Board Exam HOTS questions!)*

### 3. From $1 + \cot^2\theta = \operatorname{cosec}^2\theta$:
- $\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta - \cot^2\theta = 1$
- $(\operatorname{cosec}\theta - \cot\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta) = 1 \implies \operatorname{cosec}\theta - \cot\theta = \frac{1}{\operatorname{cosec}\theta + \cot\theta}$

title: Teacher Tip: The 4 Master Strategies to Prove ANY Identity
body:
Students often panic when asked to 'Prove the following identity'. Follow this 4-step checklist:

**Strategy 1: The Golden Escape Rule (Convert to sin and cos)**
If the question involves $\tan, \cot, \sec,$ or $\operatorname{cosec}$, convert everything into $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}, \quad \cot\theta = \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}, \quad \sec\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta}, \quad \operatorname{cosec}\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta}$$

**Strategy 2: Rationalize the Conjugate**
Whenever you see $1 \pm \sin\theta$ or $1 \pm \cos\theta$ in the denominator, multiply top and bottom by its conjugate ($1 \mp \sin\theta$ or $1 \mp \cos\theta$) to create $\cos^2\theta$ or $\sin^2\theta$!

**Strategy 3: Algebraic Factoring**
Watch out for standard algebraic expansions:
- $a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)$
- $a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)$
- $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$

**Strategy 4: Simplify LHS and RHS Separately**
If starting from LHS doesn't reach RHS directly, simplify LHS to its simplest form, then simplify RHS to its simplest form. If both equal the same expression, proof is complete!

title: NCERT Example 11: Prove (cot A - cos A) / (cot A + cos A) = (cosec A - 1) / (cosec A + 1)
body:
**Problem:** Prove that $\frac{\cot A - \cos A}{\cot A + \cos A} = \frac{\operatorname{cosec} A - 1}{\operatorname{cosec} A + 1}$.

**Proof:**
Express $\cot A$ as $\frac{\cos A}{\sin A}$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\frac{\cos A}{\sin A} - \cos A}{\frac{\cos A}{\sin A} + \cos A}$$
Factor out $\cos A$ from both numerator and denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\cos A \left(\frac{1}{\sin A} - 1\right)}{\cos A \left(\frac{1}{\sin A} + 1\right)} = \frac{\frac{1}{\sin A} - 1}{\frac{1}{\sin A} + 1}$$
Since $\frac{1}{\sin A} = \operatorname{cosec} A$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\operatorname{cosec} A - 1}{\operatorname{cosec} A + 1} = \text{RHS}$$
Hence proved!

title: Exercise 8.3 Q4(i): Prove (cosec θ - cot θ)² = (1 - cos θ) / (1 + cos θ)
body:
**Proof:**
$$\text{LHS} = (\operatorname{cosec}\theta - \cot\theta)^2 = \left(\frac{1}{\sin\theta} - \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\right)^2 = \frac{(1 - \cos\theta)^2}{\sin^2\theta}$$

$$\text{LHS} = \frac{(1 - \cos\theta)^2}{1 - \cos^2\theta} = \frac{(1 - \cos\theta)(1 - \cos\theta)}{(1 - \cos\theta)(1 + \cos\theta)}$$
Cancel $(1 - \cos\theta)$ from numerator and denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{1 - \cos\theta}{1 + \cos\theta} = \text{RHS}$$
Hence proved!

title: Exercise 8.3 Q4(ii): Prove cos A / (1 + sin A) + (1 + sin A) / cos A = 2 sec A
body:
**Proof:**
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\cos A}{1 + \sin A} + \frac{1 + \sin A}{\cos A}$$
Taking common denominator $(1 + \sin A)\cos A$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\cos^2 A + (1 + \sin A)^2}{(1 + \sin A)\cos A} = \frac{\cos^2 A + 1 + 2\sin A + \sin^2 A}{(1 + \sin A)\cos A}$$
Using $\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A = 1$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{1 + 1 + 2\sin A}{(1 + \sin A)\cos A} = \frac{2 + 2\sin A}{(1 + \sin A)\cos A} = \frac{2(1 + \sin A)}{(1 + \sin A)\cos A}$$
Cancel $(1 + \sin A)$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{2}{\cos A} = 2\sec A = \text{RHS}$$
Hence proved!

title: Exercise 8.3 Q4(iii): Prove tan θ / (1 - cot θ) + cot θ / (1 - tan θ) = 1 + sec θ cosec θ
body:
**Proof:**
Convert all ratios into $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$:
$$\frac{\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}}{1 - \frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}} + \frac{\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}}{1 - \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}} = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos\theta(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)} - \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)}$$
Take common denominator $\sin\theta\cos\theta(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)$:
$$= \frac{\sin^3\theta - \cos^3\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)}$$
Using $a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)$:
$$= \frac{(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)(\sin^2\theta + \sin\theta\cos\theta + \cos^2\theta)}{\sin\theta\cos\theta(\sin\theta - \cos\theta)}$$
$$= \frac{1 + \sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \frac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} + \frac{\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta} = \operatorname{cosec}\theta\sec\theta + 1 = \text{RHS}$$
Hence proved!

**Proof (Board Exam Master Problem):**
Divide each term of numerator and denominator by $\sin A$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\frac{\cos A}{\sin A} - 1 + \frac{1}{\sin A}}{\frac{\cos A}{\sin A} + 1 - \frac{1}{\sin A}} = \frac{\cot A + \operatorname{cosec} A - 1}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1}$$
In the numerator, substitute $1 = \operatorname{cosec}^2 A - \cot^2 A$:
$$= \frac{(\operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A) - (\operatorname{cosec}^2 A - \cot^2 A)}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1}$$
$$= \frac{(\operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A) - [(\operatorname{cosec} A - \cot A)(\operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A)]}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1}$$
Factor out $(\operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A)$:
$$= \frac{(\operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A)[1 - (\operatorname{cosec} A - \cot A)]}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1} = \frac{(\operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A)(1 - \operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A)}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1}$$
Cancel the common factor $(1 - \operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A)$:
$$= \operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A = \text{RHS}$$
Hence proved!
title_hi: प्रश्नावली 8.3 Q4(v): सिद्ध कीजिए कि (cos A - sin A + 1) / (cos A + sin A - 1) = cosec A + cot A
body_hi:
**उपपत्ति:**
अंश और हर को $\sin A$ से भाग देने पर:
$$= \frac{\cot A + \operatorname{cosec} A - 1}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1}$$
अंश में $1 = \operatorname{cosec}^2 A - \cot^2 A$ रखने पर:
$$= \frac{(\operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A)[1 - (\operatorname{cosec} A - \cot A)]}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1} = \operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A = \text{RHS}।$$
title_gu: સ્વાધ્યાય 8.3 Q4(v): સાબિત કરો કે (cos A - sin A + 1) / (cos A + sin A - 1) = cosec A + cot A
body_gu:
**સાબિતી:**
અંશ અને છેદને $\sin A$ વડે ભાગતાં:
$$= \frac{\cot A + \operatorname{cosec} A - 1}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1}$$
અંશમાં $1 = \operatorname{cosec}^2 A - \cot^2 A$ મૂકતાં:
$$= \frac{(\operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A)[1 - (\operatorname{cosec} A - \cot A)]}{\cot A - \operatorname{cosec} A + 1} = \operatorname{cosec} A + \cot A = \text{જ.બા.}$$

title: Exercise 8.3 Q4(vi): Prove √[(1 + sin A) / (1 - sin A)] = sec A + tan A
body:
**Proof:**
Multiply numerator and denominator inside the square root by $(1 + \sin A)$:
$$\text{LHS} = \sqrt{\frac{(1 + \sin A)(1 + \sin A)}{(1 - \sin A)(1 + \sin A)}} = \sqrt{\frac{(1 + \sin A)^2}{1 - \sin^2 A}}$$
Since $1 - \sin^2 A = \cos^2 A$:
$$\text{LHS} = \sqrt{\frac{(1 + \sin A)^2}{\cos^2 A}} = \frac{1 + \sin A}{\cos A} = \frac{1}{\cos A} + \frac{\sin A}{\cos A} = \sec A + \tan A = \text{RHS}$$
Hence proved!
title_hi: प्रश्नावली 8.3 Q4(vi): सिद्ध कीजिए कि √[(1 + sin A) / (1 - sin A)] = sec A + tan A
body_hi:
**उपपत्ति:**
करणी के अंदर $(1 + \sin A)$ से अंश व हर में गुणा करने पर:
$$\text{LHS} = \sqrt{\frac{(1 + \sin A)^2}{1 - \sin^2 A}} = \sqrt{\frac{(1 + \sin A)^2}{\cos^2 A}} = \frac{1 + \sin A}{\cos A} = \sec A + \tan A = \text{RHS}।$$
title_gu: સ્વાધ્યાય 8.3 Q4(vi): સાબિત કરો કે √[(1 + sin A) / (1 - sin A)] = sec A + tan A
body_gu:
**સાબિતી:**
વર્ગમૂળની અંદર $(1 + \sin A)$ વડે અંશ અને છેદને ગુણતાં:
$$\text{ડા.બા.} = \sqrt{\frac{(1 + \sin A)^2}{1 - \sin^2 A}} = \frac{1 + \sin A}{\cos A} = \sec A + \tan A = \text{જ.બા.}$$

title: Exercise 8.3 Q4(vii): Prove (sin θ - 2 sin³θ) / (2 cos³θ - cos θ) = tan θ
body:
**Proof:**
Factor out $\sin\theta$ from numerator and $\cos\theta$ from denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\sin\theta(1 - 2\sin^2\theta)}{\cos\theta(2\cos^2\theta - 1)}$$
In the numerator, substitute $1 = \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta$:
$$1 - 2\sin^2\theta = (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta) - 2\sin^2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$$
In the denominator:
$$2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 2\cos^2\theta - (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta) = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta$$
Therefore:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\sin\theta(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)}{\cos\theta(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)} = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \tan\theta = \text{RHS}$$
Hence proved!
title_hi: प्रश्नावली 8.3 Q4(vii): सिद्ध कीजिए कि (sin θ - 2 sin³θ) / (2 cos³θ - cos θ) = tan θ
body_hi:
**उपपत्ति:**
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\sin\theta(1 - 2\sin^2\theta)}{\cos\theta(2\cos^2\theta - 1)}$$
$1 = \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta$ रखने पर दोनों कोष्ठक $(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)$ बन जाते हैं:
$$= \frac{\sin\theta(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)}{\cos\theta(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)} = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \tan\theta = \text{RHS}।$$
title_gu: સ્વાધ્યાય 8.3 Q4(vii): સાબિત કરો કે (sin θ - 2 sin³θ) / (2 cos³θ - cos θ) = tan θ
body_gu:
**સાબિતી:**
$$\text{ડા.બા.} = \frac{\sin\theta(1 - 2\sin^2\theta)}{\cos\theta(2\cos^2\theta - 1)}$$
$1 = \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta$ મૂકતાં બંને કૌંસ $(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)$ બને છે:
$$= \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \tan\theta = \text{જ.બા.}$$

title: Exercise 8.3 Q4(viii): Prove (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)² = 7 + tan²A + cot²A
body:
**Proof:**
Expand both squared binomials using $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$:
$$\text{LHS} = (\sin^2 A + 2\sin A\operatorname{cosec} A + \operatorname{cosec}^2 A) + (\cos^2 A + 2\cos A\sec A + \sec^2 A)$$
Since $\sin A\operatorname{cosec} A = 1$ and $\cos A\sec A = 1$:
$$= (\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A) + 2(1) + 2(1) + \operatorname{cosec}^2 A + \sec^2 A$$
$$= 1 + 2 + 2 + \operatorname{cosec}^2 A + \sec^2 A = 5 + \operatorname{cosec}^2 A + \sec^2 A$$
Now substitute identities $\operatorname{cosec}^2 A = 1 + \cot^2 A$ and $\sec^2 A = 1 + \tan^2 A$:
$$= 5 + (1 + \cot^2 A) + (1 + \tan^2 A) = 7 + \tan^2 A + \cot^2 A = \text{RHS}$$
Hence proved!
title_hi: प्रश्नावली 8.3 Q4(viii): सिद्ध कीजिए कि (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)² = 7 + tan²A + cot²A
body_hi:
**उपपत्ति:**
विस्तार करने पर:
$$\text{LHS} = \sin^2 A + 2(1) + \operatorname{cosec}^2 A + \cos^2 A + 2(1) + \sec^2 A$$
$$= (\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A) + 4 + \operatorname{cosec}^2 A + \sec^2 A = 5 + (1 + \cot^2 A) + (1 + \tan^2 A) = 7 + \tan^2 A + \cot^2 A = \text{RHS}।$$
title_gu: સ્વાધ્યાય 8.3 Q4(viii): સાબિત કરો કે (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)² = 7 + tan²A + cot²A
body_gu:
**સાબિતી:**
વિસ્તરણ કરતાં:
$$\text{ડા.બા.} = (\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A) + 2 + 2 + \operatorname{cosec}^2 A + \sec^2 A$$
$$= 1 + 4 + (1 + \cot^2 A) + (1 + \tan^2 A) = 7 + \tan^2 A + \cot^2 A = \text{જ.બા.}$$

title: Exercise 8.3 Q4(ix): Prove (cosec A - sin A)(sec A - cos A) = 1 / (tan A + cot A)
body:
**Proof (Simplifying LHS & RHS):**
$$\text{LHS} = \left(\frac{1}{\sin A} - \sin A\right)\left(\frac{1}{\cos A} - \cos A\right) = \left(\frac{1 - \sin^2 A}{\sin A}\right)\left(\frac{1 - \cos^2 A}{\cos A}\right)$$
$$= \left(\frac{\cos^2 A}{\sin A}\right)\left(\frac{\sin^2 A}{\cos A}\right) = \cos A \sin A$$

Now simplify RHS:
$$\text{RHS} = \frac{1}{\tan A + \cot A} = \frac{1}{\frac{\sin A}{\cos A} + \frac{\cos A}{\sin A}} = \frac{1}{\frac{\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A}{\sin A\cos A}} = \frac{1}{\frac{1}{\sin A\cos A}} = \sin A\cos A$$
Since $\text{LHS} = \text{RHS} = \sin A\cos A$, the identity is proved!
title_hi: प्रश्नावली 8.3 Q4(ix): सिद्ध कीजिए कि (cosec A - sin A)(sec A - cos A) = 1 / (tan A + cot A)
body_hi:
**उपपत्ति:**
$$\text{LHS} = \left(\frac{\cos^2 A}{\sin A}\right)\left(\frac{\sin^2 A}{\cos A}\right) = \sin A\cos A$$
$$\text{RHS} = \frac{1}{\frac{\sin A}{\cos A} + \frac{\cos A}{\sin A}} = \frac{1}{\frac{\sin^2 A + \cos^2 A}{\sin A\cos A}} = \sin A\cos A$$
चूँकि LHS = RHS, अतः सिद्ध हुआ!
title_gu: સ્વાધ્યાય 8.3 Q4(ix): સાબિત કરો કે (cosec A - sin A)(sec A - cos A) = 1 / (tan A + cot A)
body_gu:
**સાબિતી:**
$$\text{ડા.બા.} = \left(\frac{\cos^2 A}{\sin A}\right)\left(\frac{\sin^2 A}{\cos A}\right) = \sin A\cos A$$
$$\text{જ.બા.} = \frac{1}{\frac{\sin A}{\cos A} + \frac{\cos A}{\sin A}} = \frac{1}{\frac{1}{\sin A\cos A}} = \sin A\cos A$$
ડા.બા. = જ.બા. હોવાથી સાબિત થાય છે!

title: Exercise 8.3 Q4(x): Prove (1 + tan²A) / (1 + cot²A) = [(1 - tan A) / (1 - cot A)]² = tan²A
body:
**Proof:**
**Part 1:**
$$\frac{1 + \tan^2 A}{1 + \cot^2 A} = \frac{\sec^2 A}{\operatorname{cosec}^2 A} = \frac{1/\cos^2 A}{1/\sin^2 A} = \frac{\sin^2 A}{\cos^2 A} = \tan^2 A$$

**Part 2:**
$$\left(\frac{1 - \tan A}{1 - \cot A}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{1 - \tan A}{1 - \frac{1}{\tan A}}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{1 - \tan A}{\frac{\tan A - 1}{\tan A}}\right)^2$$
$$= \left(\frac{1 - \tan A}{-(1 - \tan A)} \times \tan A\right)^2 = (-\tan A)^2 = \tan^2 A$$
Thus, both expressions equal $\tan^2 A$. Hence proved!
title_hi: प्रश्नावली 8.3 Q4(x): सिद्ध कीजिए कि (1 + tan²A) / (1 + cot²A) = [(1 - tan A) / (1 - cot A)]² = tan²A
body_hi:
**उपपत्ति:**
**भाग 1:** $\frac{\sec^2 A}{\operatorname{cosec}^2 A} = \frac{\sin^2 A}{\cos^2 A} = \tan^2 A$।
**भाग 2:** $\left(\frac{1 - \tan A}{1 - 1/\tan A}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{1 - \tan A}{\frac{\tan A - 1}{\tan A}}\right)^2 = (-\tan A)^2 = \tan^2 A$।
अतः दोनों व्यंजक $\tan^2 A$ के बराबर हैं!
title_gu: સ્વાધ્યાય 8.3 Q4(x): સાબિત કરો કે (1 + tan²A) / (1 + cot²A) = [(1 - tan A) / (1 - cot A)]² = tan²A
body_gu:
**સાબિતી:**
**ભાગ 1:** $\frac{\sec^2 A}{\operatorname{cosec}^2 A} = \frac{\sin^2 A}{\cos^2 A} = \tan^2 A$.
**ભાગ 2:** $\left(\frac{1 - \tan A}{1 - 1/\tan A}\right)^2 = (-\tan A)^2 = \tan^2 A$.
બંને પદો $\tan^2 A$ બરાબર સાબિત થાય છે!

question: Board HOTS: If sec θ + tan θ = p, what is the value of sin θ?
explanation:
We know sec²θ - tan²θ = 1 ⇒ (sec θ - tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = 1.
Given sec θ + tan θ = p ⇒ sec θ - tan θ = 1/p.
Adding the two equations: 2 sec θ = p + 1/p = (p² + 1)/p ⇒ sec θ = (p² + 1)/2p.
Subtracting the two equations: 2 tan θ = p - 1/p = (p² - 1)/p ⇒ tan θ = (p² - 1)/2p.
Therefore, sin θ = tan θ / sec θ = [(p² - 1)/2p] / [(p² + 1)/2p] = (p² - 1) / (p² + 1).
question_hi: बोर्ड परीक्षा HOTS: यदि sec θ + tan θ = p, तो sin θ का मान क्या होगा?
explanation_hi:
sec θ + tan θ = p तथा sec θ - tan θ = 1/p।
जोड़ने पर: sec θ = (p² + 1)/2p।
घटाने पर: tan θ = (p² - 1)/2p।
sin θ = tan θ / sec θ = (p² - 1) / (p² + 1)।
question_gu: બોર્ડ HOTS પ્રશ્ન: જો sec θ + tan θ = p હોય, તો sin θ નું મૂલ્ય શું થાય?
explanation_gu:
sec θ + tan θ = p અને sec θ - tan θ = 1/p.
સરવાળો કરતાં: sec θ = (p² + 1)/2p.
બાદબાકી કરતાં: tan θ = (p² - 1)/2p.
sin θ = tan θ / sec θ = (p² - 1) / (p² + 1).

question: Board HOTS: If x = a sin θ + b cos θ and y = a cos θ - b sin θ, find the value of x² + y².
explanation:
x² = (a sin θ + b cos θ)² = a² sin²θ + b² cos²θ + 2ab sin θ cos θ.
y² = (a cos θ - b sin θ)² = a² cos²θ + b² sin²θ - 2ab sin θ cos θ.
Adding x² and y²:
x² + y² = a²(sin²θ + cos²θ) + b²(cos²θ + sin²θ) + (2ab sin θ cos θ - 2ab sin θ cos θ)
= a²(1) + b²(1) + 0 = a² + b².
question_hi: बोर्ड परीक्षा HOTS: यदि x = a sin θ + b cos θ और y = a cos θ - b sin θ, तो x² + y² का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation_hi:
x² और y² का विस्तार करके जोड़ने पर:
x² + y² = a²(sin²θ + cos²θ) + b²(cos²θ + sin²θ) = a² + b²।
question_gu: બોર્ડ HOTS પ્રશ્ન: જો x = a sin θ + b cos θ અને y = a cos θ - b sin θ હોય, તો x² + y² નું મૂલ્ય શોધો.
explanation_gu:
x² અને y² નો સરવાળો કરતાં:
x² + y² = a²(sin²θ + cos²θ) + b²(cos²θ + sin²θ) = a² + b².

question: Board HOTS: If sin θ + sin²θ = 1, find the value of the expression (cos²θ + cos⁴θ).
explanation:
Given: sin θ + sin²θ = 1 ⇒ sin θ = 1 - sin²θ.
Since 1 - sin²θ = cos²θ, we have:
sin θ = cos²θ.
Squaring both sides:
sin²θ = (cos²θ)² = cos⁴θ.
Now substitute into the required expression:
cos²θ + cos⁴θ = sin θ + sin²θ.
Since sin θ + sin²θ is given as 1, the value is exactly 1!
question_hi: बोर्ड परीक्षा HOTS: यदि sin θ + sin²θ = 1, तो व्यंजक (cos²θ + cos⁴θ) का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation_hi:
दिया है: sin θ = 1 - sin²θ = cos²θ।
दोनों पक्षों का वर्ग करने पर: sin²θ = cos⁴θ।
अतः cos²θ + cos⁴θ = sin θ + sin²θ = 1।
question_gu: બોર્ડ HOTS પ્રશ્ન: જો sin θ + sin²θ = 1 હોય, તો (cos²θ + cos⁴θ) નું મૂલ્ય શોધો.
explanation_gu:
આપેલ છે: sin θ = 1 - sin²θ = cos²θ.
બંને બાજુ વર્ગ કરતાં: sin²θ = cos⁴θ.
તેથી cos²θ + cos⁴θ = sin θ + sin²θ = 1.

title: Reflection: The Socratic Triangle of Understanding
body:
Take a quiet moment to reflect on your journey through Chapter 8:

1. **The Core Philosophy:** Trigonometry is not about memorizing mysterious syllables (sin, cos, tan). It is the simple recognition that in any right triangle with a fixed angle, the ratios of sides never change, whether the triangle is drawn on a tiny postage stamp or connects three stars in deep space.
2. **The Golden Bridge:** When you know one angle and one side, you can find ALL sides and angles! This is the superpower that makes modern engineering possible.
3. **Can you explain to a friend:** Why is $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta$ always equal to $1$? (Because it is literally the Pythagoras theorem $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ divided by $c^2$!).
title_hi: चिंतन: समझ का सुकराती त्रिकोण

3. **क्या आप अपने मित्र को समझा सकते हैं:** $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta$ हमेशा 1 क्यों होता है? (क्योंकि यह वास्तव में पाइथागोरस प्रमेय $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ को $c^2$ से भाग देने पर प्राप्त होता है!)।

title: Connection: Where Does Trigonometry Lead in Science & Life?
body:
Trigonometry is the mathematical language of waves, cycles, and space:

- **Chapter 9 (Some Applications of Trigonometry):** You will use $\tan\theta$ and $\sin\theta$ to find heights of lighthouses, distances of ships at sea, and widths of rivers using Angles of Elevation and Depression!
- **Physics (Vectors & Projectiles):** Breaking velocity into horizontal ($v\cos\theta$) and vertical ($v\sin\theta$) components.
- **Audio & Sound Waves:** Every musical note, speech signal, and radio wave is a pure sine wave ($y = A\sin(\omega t)$).
- **Computer Graphics & Game Development:** Character rotation, camera angles in Unreal Engine and Unity, and ray tracing in games all run on trigonometric matrices!
- **Space Exploration (ISRO & NASA):** Orbital mechanics, satellite trajectories, and planetary alignment calculations rely 100% on trigonometry.

title: Mastery Blueprint: Guaranteed Board Exam Success Formula
body:
To score full marks (100%) in Introduction to Trigonometry in your Board Exam:

1. **Label the Diagram First:** Always draw the right triangle clearly and mark the reference angle $\theta$ before writing down ratios. Never confuse opposite side with adjacent side!
2. **The 3-Second Verification:** Remember that $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ can NEVER be greater than $1$. If you get $\sin\theta = 5/4$, stop immediately and check your arithmetic!
3. **Proving Identities:** Write 'LHS =' clearly. Convert all composite ratios to $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ if you don't immediately see a direct identity.
4. **Rationalizing Denominators:** Always rationalize square roots in final answers (write $\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$ instead of $\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}$).
5. **Unit Discipline:** Check if sides have units (cm, m). Angles must always have the degree symbol ($^\circ$).
title_hi: मास्टरी ब्लूप्रिंट: बोर्ड परीक्षा में शत-प्रतिशत सफलता का फॉर्मूला
body_hi:
बोर्ड परीक्षा में त्रिकोणमिति में शत-प्रतिशत अंक प्राप्त करने की महत्वपूर्ण रणनीतियाँ:

1. **चित्र अवश्य बनाएँ:** अनुपात लिखने से पहले समकोण त्रिभुज बनाएँ और अभीष्ट कोण को स्पष्ट रूप से अंकित करें। सम्मुख और संलग्न भुजा में कभी भ्रमित न हों!
2. **3 सेकंड की त्वरित जाँच:** $\sin\theta$ और $\cos\theta$ का मान कभी भी 1 से अधिक नहीं हो सकता। यदि आपका मान $5/4$ आए, तो तुरंत अपनी गणना पुनः जाँचें!
3. **सर्वसमिका सिद्ध करना:** स्पष्ट रूप से 'LHS =' लिखें। यदि सीधा सूत्र न दिखे तो सभी पदों को $\sin$ और $\cos$ में बदल दें।
4. **अंतिम उत्तर का परिमेयकरण:** अंतिम उत्तर में हर में अपरिमेय संख्या न छोड़ें।
5. **इकाई का ध्यान रखें:** भुजाओं की इकाइयाँ (सेमी, मीटर) और कोणों पर डिग्री ($^\circ$) का चिह्न अवश्य लगाएँ।
title_gu: માસ્ટરી બ્લુપ્રિન્ટ: બોર્ડ પરીક્ષામાં સંપૂર્ણ ગુણ મેળવવાની ચાવી
body_gu:
બોર્ડ પરીક્ષામાં ત્રિકોણમિતિમાં પૂરા ગુણ મેળવવાની શ્રેષ્ઠ વ્યૂહરચના:

1. **આકૃતિ અનિવાર્ય દોરો:** ગુણોત્તર લખતાં પહેલાં કાટકોણ ત્રિકોણ દોરી સંદર્ભ ખૂણો દર્શાવો. સામેની અને પાસેની બાજુમાં ક્યારેય ગૂંચવાશો નહીં!
2. **ઝડપી ચકાસણી:** $\sin\theta$ અને $\cos\theta$ નું મૂલ્ય ક્યારેય 1 કરતાં મોટું ન હોઈ શકે. જો જવાબ 1 થી મોટો આવે તો તરત ગણતરી ફરી તપાસો!
3. **નિત્યસમની સાબિતી:** સ્પષ્ટપણે 'ડા.બા. =' લખો. સીધો નિત્યસમ ન દેખાય તો બધા પદોને $\sin$ અને $\cos$ માં ફેરવી નાખો.
4. **છેદનું સંમેયીકરણ:** અંતિમ જવાબમાં છેદમાં અસંમેય સંખ્યા ન રહેવી જોઈએ.
5. **એકમોની કાળજી:** લંબાઈના એકમ (સેમી, મીટર) અને ખૂણા માટે અંશ ($^\circ$) દર્શાવવાનું ક્યારેય ચૂકશો નહીં.
